background_notes.fact: If a vector space W over a field has finite dimension n and (u_i) indexed by a finite set J of cardinality n is linearly independent, then this family is a basis of W.

background_notes.justification: Start with a basis of n vectors, which exists by the given finite dimension. Insert the independent u_i one by one: expansion of the next u_i in the current basis has a nonzero coefficient on a basis vector outside the previously inserted vectors, since otherwise independence would fail. Solve for that basis vector and exchange it for u_i; spanning and independence are preserved. After n such exchanges the basis consists exactly of the u_i. Apply this with W=V, J=I and u_i=e_i.

background_notes.fact: For natural m,r, with 0!=1 and an empty product equal to 1, product_{a=1}^r(m+a)/r! = binom(m+r,r) is a nonnegative integer. Here binom(N,r), for 0<=r<=N, is the number of r-element subsets of an N-element set, equivalently N!/(r!(N-r)!). Every natural factorial is a positive integer and hence is nonzero as a complex scalar.

grounds.reason: H003 gives integer lambda>=0.

background_notes.justification: For N=m+r, ordered selections of r distinct elements from an N-element set number N(N-1)...(N-r+1). Each r-element subset has exactly r! such orderings. Thus this product divided by r! is the integer subset count; reversing its factors gives (m+1)...(m+r)/r!. For r=0 both counts and products equal 1. Factorial positivity follows by induction from 0!=1 and (s+1)!=(s+1)s!. These facts justify the two binomial identifications and integrality. The remaining generator coefficients lambda-i+1, i+1 and lambda-2i are visibly integers, and the zero branches have integer coefficient zero.

background_notes.justification: For an injective R-linear map R^a -> R^b, extend its matrix to Q. A nonzero vector in the kernel over Q could be multiplied by a common nonzero integer denominator to give a nonzero kernel vector over R, a contradiction. Thus the extension is injective and a<=b by finite linear algebra. Over Q the same inequality follows by elimination on a matrix. From a finite spanning list delete each vector dependent on the retained vectors; the resulting independent spanning list is a basis. Isomorphisms carry bases to bases, and finite basis cardinality is invariant by the injective dimension inequality. This also identifies natural-valued module rank with n for a finite free basis.

background_notes.fact: For prime integer p and every nonzero rational q, there exist eta in Z and a unit u of R=Z_(p) such that q=p^eta u. For a nonempty finite family of such exponents, its minimum nu is attained, and p^(eta_j-nu) belongs to R for each j.

background_notes.justification: Write q=A/B with nonzero integers A,B. Repeatedly remove factors p from A and B; this terminates because their nonzero absolute values decrease at each division by p>=2. Write A=p^s A' and B=p^t B', with A',B' prime to p. Then eta=s-t and u=A'/B'; both u and its inverse lie in R. A finite nonempty list of integers has an attained minimum. Each eta_j-nu is nonnegative, so the corresponding power of p is integral and belongs to R. This verifies the factorization and minimum step already used by S004–S005.
